PullRequest.Title: [cherry-pick] Enable Modern UI Update by default
PullRequest.Body:
Cherry-pick of #337013 from `main`.

## Summary

- enable `workbench.experimental.modernUI` by default while preserving explicit user and workspace opt-outs
- retain the automatic experiment metadata for the staged rollout
- include the Modern UI compatibility fixes for the chat model picker and terminal persistence smoke tests

## Validation

- verified the backport patch ID exactly matches the merged PR diff
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/browser/workbench.contribution.ts test/automation/src/chat.ts test/smoke/src/areas/terminal/terminal-persistence.test.ts`
- `cd test/smoke && npm run compile`
- repository pre-commit hygiene checks
- original PR Electron smoke tests passed on macOS, Linux, and Windows

Scenarios.Scenario: Fresh workbench startup or window reload for users without an explicit Modern UI preference
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration resolution now yields true, so initial workbench class construction and the BlockRestore ModernUIContribution apply Modern UI classes and global dimensions before restore continues. The styles are already bundled; no network, filesystem, subprocess, database, or IPC operation is added.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Workbench DOM size, visible editor groups, open tabs, and auxiliary windows. Initial class application is once per existing container, while CSS matching/layout scales with the rendered workbench.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All configuration reads, class toggles, and initial DOM/layout setup execute serially on the renderer UI thread. The constructor seeds the current layout-affecting state before update, so it does not schedule an extra workbench relayout merely because the default is enabled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The resolved configuration value is read through the existing configuration service. Cold and warm startup use the same setting key; explicit user/workspace false values still override the default. There is no new cache, miss path, or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the diff broadens the existing Modern UI render/layout path to default users; low confidence that this path is slower, because the changed line adds no operation and available repository evidence does not demonstrate a regression mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Modern UI changes CSS and geometry for the full workbench, but the repository's dedicated Modern UI CSS benchmark and audit document bounded selectors and no active Modern UI invalidation hazards. No before/after classic-versus-modern timing is present, so a performance degradation cannot be established from the default flip alone.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The default change makes an existing presentation path common but does not itself prove increased startup latency, CPU, memory, I/O, or rendering cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Routine Modern UI rendering, resizing, tab switching, and side bar/panel toggles after startup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: UI interactions synchronously run existing layout code and browser style/layout/paint under the now-default Modern UI classes. No external boundary must complete; browser rendering is the critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of rendered DOM nodes, visible tabs, groups, and layout interactions. Existing tab and pane code already bounds visible DOM through its normal components.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Renderer work is serialized on the UI thread. Layout remains one existing pass per resize or layout action; the default flip does not add a new listener, loop, timer, or concurrent task per interaction.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CSS is bundled and already loaded regardless of setting. Style calculations use directly toggled root/module classes rather than a newly introduced runtime cache. No cold/warm cache difference or coalescing change is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in critical-path reachability and UI-thread serialization; insufficient confidence that performance worsens rather than merely changes styling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Rounded clipping, borders, and connected-tab pseudo-elements may alter paint cost, but no changed selector or measured classic-to-modern regression identifies a concrete scaling mechanism. The checked CSS performance document reports a dedicated warmup/measurement suite and specifically records no active Modern UI selector hazards.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Enabling an existing mode is not enough to infer rendering jank without evidence that its CSS/layout path materially costs more.

Scenarios.Scenario: Chat model-configuration smoke tests widening the auxiliary bar
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When the config button is hidden, automation enumerates top-level workbench vertical sashes and requests each bounding box before issuing the existing mouse drag, then waits 300 ms for ResizeObserver relayout. These browser-automation calls are on the test's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Playwright locator enumeration and one boundingBox request for each top-level vertical sash
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One locator enumeration plus S sequential geometry requests per retry, where S is the small number of top-level workbench vertical sashes; normally one retry is sufficient after the drag. The helper is reached by the model-configuration smoke scenarios, not product use.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The test derived the sash point directly from the already-fetched auxiliary-bar box and issued no sash enumeration or per-sash geometry requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The geometry requests must finish before the drag, adding bounded test-only latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Mouse move/down/move/up automation commands to resize the auxiliary bar
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Five mouse commands per retry, unchanged from before except that coordinates come from the selected sash bounds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same five mouse commands were sent using the auxiliary-bar edge as the sash coordinate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The drag must complete before the model picker can expand.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of top-level workbench vertical sashes and retries until the config button becomes visible.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The sash bounding-box requests are awaited serially within each retry. Retries are serialized and bounded by the existing 20-second deadline and 300 ms delay.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No sash geometry is cached across retries because layout changes after each drag; recomputing coordinates is appropriate. The visible-button common path returns before enumeration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the additional sequential automation calls and their bounded cardinality; high confidence that the impact is confined to tests and too small to meet the review threshold.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of top-level vertical sashes varies by layout, but it is structurally small and the path is limited to two smoke-test helper entry points. There is no product-user impact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff adds bounded test-only IPC to make sash selection compatible with floating panels; it does not create a realistic product performance regression or meaningful unbounded CI cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Terminal persistence smoke test across window reload and detach/attach
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test still produces 100 terminal lines, performs exactly one reload or detach/attach, focuses the terminal, waits for replay, and sends the continuation input. Moving focus before the replay wait changes ordering only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open Quick Access, select the exact Developer: Reload Window command, and trigger one Electron window reload
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one command invocation and one window reload in the window-reload variant.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The test invoked the same reload through the internal command ID; the diff changes command matching and keeps Quick Access open so command selection survives the reload transition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The reload remains the dominant required boundary before terminal replay assertions proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing integrated terminal launches a Node producer process and emits 100 sequence lines
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One terminal process per test variant, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical producer process and output cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Production finishes before the reconnect branch and therefore remains on the setup critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed 100-line sequence and two fixed reconnect variants.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The test steps remain serial. Terminal output production is complete before reconnect, and replay, focus, and continuation are awaited in sequence.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is introduced or invalidated. The quick-access command search uses existing command registration state, and terminal replay uses the existing persistence buffer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that no expensive-boundary cardinality or concurrency changed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Reload duration depends on host load, but boundary count and concurrency are unchanged. The reordered focus call is local automation work and does not add polling or repeated reloads.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The changes preserve one reload/detach operation and only adjust automation matching and wait ordering.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and all diff hunks. The production default flip broadens an existing Modern UI render path but provides no concrete evidence of additional work frequency, unbounded retention, boundary fan-out, or measurable rendering regression. The only newly introduced boundary fan-out is small, deadline-bounded, and confined to smoke-test automation.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
